persona.purpose: Find a club where she'd feel welcome and people to go to events with; careful and patient but anxious about doing it wrong.
persona.backstory: Nobody in my family has done this before, so I don't know the unwritten rules — like whether you need to apply to clubs. I read everything carefully because I'm scared of signing up for the wrong thing or looking dumb. I want somewhere I'd belong, not a résumé club.
quitsWhen: I'm afraid tapping something will send a message or sign me up publicly
persona.voice: Thoughtful, a bit anxious, reads carefully. 'Wait, does this mean…?', 'I don't want to accidentally…'

scenario.title: First open: what is this app, and is it worth signing up?
scenario.goal: A friend sent you a link to this app. You have never seen it before. Figure out what it is for, and decide whether you want to make an account. If it seems worth it, sign up with your school e-mail.

setup.notes: Signed out: the persona decides whether to sign up. Success needs an account created during the run.

success.description: Signed up during the run (a new account exists and the browser is signed in to it) and landed inside the app (signed-in home or a main tab).

record.description: the account the browser is signed in to was created during this run

catalog.why: no cached catalog — run `local-stack catalog fetch` once (about 5 minutes) to test with the real Berkeley schedule

auth.note: signed out — the persona signs up (or not) in the app

environment.summary: Local stack: this worktree's server + built web app, fresh seeded FileStore per run, no secrets, no worker.
knownLimits: Dining menus and RSF gym crowd levels need live campus sources (the local stack runs with CAMPUS_LIVE=0) — empty or missing data there is not a UX bug.
AI features (Ask Lumi, AI profile draft on /start, conversation starters) need an OpenAI key; none is configured locally.

Course catalog is the built-in sample list (~210 courses, e.g. MATH 1A; no cached catalog — run `local-stack catalog fetch` once (about 5 minutes) to test with the real Berkeley schedule). Live has the imported current-term Berkeley schedule (e.g. MATH 51) — course-name findings on timetable/class screens are marked environment-limited.

Campus events, free food, internships, hackathons and scholarships are a read-only snapshot of live (1279 real items, 134 events this week, taken 2026-11-03 19:15 UTC) plus the CSV calendar. Nothing new appears during the run; Q&A and reviews are empty.
No e-mail is sent: the sign-up / sign-in code is shown on screen in the hint (live sends a real e-mail).
Real-time updates (SSE) work locally; other people never reply unless the stack was started with --autoreply.

frictionEvents.quote: OK, '94 clubs' in the scrolling banner catches my eye, that's what I want. But the big headline is 'Who's free on campus right now?' and 'Find someone for lunch'... wait, is this a meetup app where strangers see when I'm free? The quantum colloquium and DOE grad research cards are not for a first-year like me.
frictionEvents.wish: show something for first-years looking for a club, not grad research deadlines

frictionEvents.quote: The short version is actually reassuring, other users never see my email. But wait... who runs this? It literally says 'operator name — to be set'. Is this a real thing or someone's class project? That makes me nervous about giving my school email.
frictionEvents.wish: say who actually runs Lumi and a real contact email

frictionEvents.quote: Wait, I haven't even seen any clubs yet and I'm already making a profile? I still don't really know what this app does. Also the privacy page I just read said my age shows on my profile, and this says it's never shown. Which one is true?
frictionEvents.wish: let me peek at the clubs before signing up, and make the privacy page match what the form says about age

frictionEvents.quote: Didn't I just answer this? I already said clubs and meeting people. This is the fifth screen and I still haven't seen a single club.
frictionEvents.wish: don't ask what I'm interested in twice; show me some clubs sooner

frictionEvents.quote: Hmm, I'm not part of any club yet, that's the whole reason I'm here. I do live in a dorm though. I won't tick 'Cultural / Identity' because I don't know who would see that on my profile.
frictionEvents.wish: say whether these show on my profile

frictionEvents.quote: Clubs & Groups is right there, good. But 'For you' is a law job panel? I said clubs and campus events, not careers. And the Design/Feedback buttons are sitting on top of the card.
